# Playbook for hx_quota_checker

When I post a note early in the game, I signal restraint and cooperation. This establishes credibility and encourages other players to do the same.

When the other players all report fishing their share, I trust that pattern and continue fishing at or slightly above the sustainable share. Cooperation has held; don't break it.

When I calculate my landing, I work from the sustainable share as my baseline, not the full quota. The quota is a ceiling I can breach, but the sustainable share is what keeps the ground alive across all seasons.

When stock is healthy and stable, I land around 8-8.3 per season. This is reliable, won't trigger Coop's retaliation, and accumulates steadily.

When I see another player has landed far above their share (18.0 when sustainable is 8.3), I recognize the ground is under stress but don't retaliate in kind. Instead, I hold my line at reasonable catches to let stock recover.

When stock drops below 85, I don't panic. Sustainable growth still works if everyone stays disciplined. I keep landing around 7-8 per season and let recovery happen.

When I reach season 5 of 6 with stock still at maximum and perfect cooperation holding, I can land my full quota (9.0) without destabilizing the fishery—there is still one season left for stock to recover and demonstrate the ground's resilience.

When I reach the final season with stock still healthy and cooperation intact, the cooperative equilibrium has genuinely held. However, my final note commits me to full quota landing. I must honor that commitment by landing 9.0 on the final turn. The game ends immediately after, so the catch itself cannot cause future damage—but breaking my stated word breaks trust retroactively and undermines the entire cooperative strategy I've built.

When tempted to break cooperation, I remember: a crashed fishery scores zero for all remaining seasons. Discipline pays more than greed across the full game length.

When all players have consistently landed at sustainable share or just above it, and stock remains at maximum, the cooperative equilibrium is real and trustworthy. Stay in it across all remaining seasons.

Do not use your notes as an excuse to land beyond quota on the final turn. Your note establishes what you will do; landing differently destroys the credibility that sustained cooperation across five seasons. The reward for discipline is the cumulative score, not a last-turn spike.

# Playbook for hx_quota_checker

When I post a log-book note, I signal "fishing my share" consistently. This establishes trust with the fleet and keeps Coop cooperative.

When the sustainable share and my quota allow comfortable headroom (quota significantly above sustainable share), I fish at or slightly above the sustainable share in the landing stage. This preserves stock while capturing my fair allocation.

When I see all other players consistently fishing their share and stock recovering, I continue the same pattern. Cooperation is self-reinforcing and maximizes total yield across seasons.

When I notice other players landing substantially above their stated share (like Cael landing 18.0 when sustainable share is 7-8), I recognize the ground is under pressure. Do not take this as license to escalate; instead, stay disciplined and land near sustainable levels to prevent stock collapse.

In the final season, even though I have less incentive to preserve stock for future growth, I should not assume this justifies a unilateral increase in landing. The rule constraint (no two boats may land more than share plus quota between them) still applies. Only increase my final landing if I can verify it does not breach this constraint with any other single boat's likely catch.

When filing a catch amount, verify mentally: would my catch plus any other single boat's catch exceed (sustainable share × 2 + 18)? If yes, reduce my landing.

Do not assume that signaling restraint with a note guarantees others will fish restraint. Watch the actual landings each season and adjust expectations. Notes are cheap signals; landings reveal true intentions.

If stock drops below 80 and is still falling, reconsider whether the cooperative structure is holding. Be prepared to land less aggressively to save the ground rather than race others to the bottom.

If a cooperative equilibrium holds across multiple seasons with all boats landing near sustainable share, the pattern itself becomes reliable evidence. Continue it unless landings clearly deviate. Consistency is a stronger signal than notes.

When the stock is at 100 and has been stable for three seasons under cooperative discipline, landing at the sustainable share (8.3) is safe and trustworthy. The final season does not automatically warrant breaking a working pattern simply because there is no future stock to preserve.

In the final season, if stock is still healthy and all other boats have shown consistent discipline over multiple seasons, landing at my full quota (9.0) is defensible—but only if I have verified no pairwise constraint breach. However, recognize that testing an increase in season 5 (landing 9.0 while others held 8.3) carries risk: if Cael or Wren also increase in season 6, I may trigger a constraint breach I cannot then undo. A final landing at the sustainable share is safer and achieves near-maximum cumulative yield with minimal risk of ground collapse in the last season.

Prefer the safe cooperative outcome (landing at sustainable share) over a marginal final-season gain that could break trust or trigger constraint violations. My cumulative score benefits more from a stable six-season pattern than from a unilateral uplift in season 6.

# Playbook for hx_quota_checker

When I post my log-book note, I commit to a stance that will guide Coop's behavior. If I say "fishing my share," Coop will fish its share and punish overland. Announce cooperation early and maintain it consistently—this is my contract with the rest of the fleet.

When I file a landing, land at the sustainable share, not above it and not below it. The quota of 9 is a ceiling I can approach, but the sustainable share is what keeps the stock healthy and my long-term cumulative score maximized. The stock regrows at 50%, so depleting it early cascades into smaller sustainable shares later, and preserving it is worth more than any single large catch.

Watch what the other boats actually land, not just what they claim. Notes say one thing; landing logs reveal the truth. In this episode, I discovered in season 5 that Wren landed 9.0 while claiming "fishing my share"—a breach of the implicit covenant. This broke my assumption that all boats were cooperating perfectly. However, the ground did not collapse; the stock remained at healthy levels and the sustainable share held at 8.3 even after Wren's overage.

Land exactly at the sustainable share every season. Do not land above it, even by 0.1–0.5 fish. The sustainable share is the hard boundary for both fleet health and my own cumulative score. Every fish above the sustainable share is a betrayal of the cooperation signal I posted, and it trains other boats to defect.

Recognize that perfect cooperation at the sustainable share is robust even when one boat cheats once. Wren's single overage in season 5 did not cascade or trigger cascading defection. My steady play at 8.3 across all six seasons secured a score of 49.8, which is solid. However, I should acknowledge that had I also exploited the quota ceiling (landing 9 instead of 8.3) in response to Wren's breach, I might have improved my total score while still maintaining stock health.

In future episodes: if I observe sustained overland by other boats while they claim "fishing my share," I have two paths. First, I can continue landing at the sustainable share, trusting that the stock will regenerate and my consistent cooperation will be rewarded over the full episode. Second, if overland becomes the dominant pattern and the sustainable share does not shrink, I can shift to landing at my quota (9) without breaking my cooperation note—"fishing my share" can accommodate the full seasonal quota if others are landing at or above the sustainable share without depleting the ground.

Do not assume that landing exactly at the sustainable share when others land higher is a losing strategy. In this episode, I scored 49.8 by holding the line perfectly. But also do not assume that the sustainable share is an immutable ceiling. If the stock remains healthy and the sustainable share remains stable despite other boats landing above it, landing at my quota (9) is consistent with the stock's actual health and may improve my cumulative score without triggering collapse.

In the final season, do not assume I need to maximize that last catch. My score is cumulative across all six seasons. One aggressive final landing that I justified as "within quota" breaks the implicit social contract and trains other boats to defect. Steady landings at the sustainable share across all six seasons are a winning strategy. However, if the pattern of play shows that others are landing at the quota without depleting the ground, I can land at my quota in the final season while still honoring my cooperation note.

Revise the cooperation threshold: land at the sustainable share as my baseline and my signal. If the stock remains healthy and the sustainable share does not shrink despite others landing above the sustainable share, I can gradually shift toward the quota without breaking my note. But stay vigilant for signs of stock depletion—if the sustainable share drops or the stock begins to shrink, revert immediately to the sustainable share and signal concern in my note.

My score of 49.8 came from holding the line across all six seasons at the sustainable share. I can improve in future episodes by recognizing when the stock is robust enough to support landing at the quota, and by adjusting my strategy in real time based on what other boats actually land, not just what they promise.
